articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on November 13, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities.
These actions aim to disrupt the financial networks of those who facilitate illicit drug trade and support terrorist organizations globally.
Further details regarding the specific individuals and entities designated, as well as the implications of these actions, are available on the Treasury website.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran Designation Update
body: OFAC released an update to its Iran designations on November 9, 2026. This action follows ongoing efforts to address Iran's nuclear program, support for terrorism, and human rights violations.
The update includes modifications to existing listings and may introduce new individuals or entities to the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List.
The Treasury Department continues to emphasize the importance of vigilance in transactions related to Iran to prevent sanctions evasion.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Eight Canada-Based Money Services Businesses for Iran-Related Activities
body: On November 6, 2026, OFAC imposed blocking sanctions against eight Canada-based money services businesses. These entities were designated for allegedly operating in the digital asset sector of the Iranian economy.

According to OFAC, these businesses are involved in exchanging Iranian rials and other currencies for digital assets, with many reportedly dealing with sanctioned Iranian cryptocurrency exchanges and digital asset addresses linked to the IRGC.
This action was coordinated with FinCEN, Canada's financial intelligence unit, and the Drug Enforcement Administration, highlighting international cooperation in combating sanctions evasion.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Cuba Entities, and Publishes Cuba-related Determination
body: OFAC announced new designations on November 5, 2026, targeting cyber-related and transnational criminal organizations, as well as entities and individuals connected to Cuba.
The designations include two individuals, six entities, and two vessels added to the SDN List under E.O. 14404, with individuals listed in Cuba and Panama, and entities in Cuba, China, and Panama.
Additionally, OFAC published a Cuba-related determination, further restricting transactions and dealings with the Cuban government and its supporters.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related Designations, Updates Listings, Issues Alert, and Amends Venezuela GL
body: On November 4, 2026, OFAC announced new Iran-related designations, updates to certain Iran-related listings, and the publication of an Iran-related OFAC Alert.

The United States imposed blocking sanctions against five individuals in India and Russia and ten entities in India, Singapore, and Turkey under E.O. 13902 or the Iran-related conventional-arms sanctions authority.

OFAC also issued Venezuela General License 5AA, replacing General License 5Z and postponing until December 18, 2026, the authorization for specified transactions involving the PDVSA 2020 8.5 percent bond.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License
body: On October 29, 2026, OFAC issued an amended Iran-related General License. This amendment modifies existing authorizations for certain transactions involving Iran.
The specifics of the amended license aim to clarify permissible activities while maintaining the overall sanctions framework against Iran.
Entities engaging in Iran-related transactions are advised to review the updated guidance carefully to ensure compliance.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Imposes North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo-Related Designations
body: OFAC announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting individuals and entities connected to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
These actions are part of ongoing efforts to counter proliferation financing from North Korea and address human rights abuses and corruption in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The designations aim to disrupt illicit financial networks and promote accountability in both regions.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs Regarding Blocking and Rejecting Transactions and Filing Reports
body: On October 26, 2026, OFAC issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.
These amendments provide updated guidance and clarifications for financial institutions and other entities on their obligations under OFAC sanctions programs.
The revisions aim to enhance compliance and streamline reporting processes for blocked or rejected transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses
body: On October 21, 2026, OFAC announced new Iran-related designations, alongside removals of certain Belarus and North Korea designations.
The action also included the issuance of new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended Frequently Asked Questions.
These measures reflect a dynamic approach to sanctions, adjusting to evolving geopolitical circumstances and specific compliance needs.

articles.headline: OCC Imposes Record $750 Million Civil Money Penalty on Bank of America for BSA/AML Failures
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) announced a $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America, N.A., for widespread breakdowns in its Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program.

This penalty is the largest in OCC history and stems from the bank's deficient transaction monitoring system, which failed to properly monitor trillions of dollars in transactions and resulted in numerous late suspicious activity reports (SARs) involving billions of dollars.
The OCC found that despite a December 2024 cease-and-desist order, the bank continued to exhibit widespread internal control deficiencies, posing a threat to U.S. national and economic security.

articles.headline: OCC Assesses $350 Million Civil Money Penalty Against American Express National Bank for BSA/AML Deficiencies
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) announced a cease-and-desist order and a $350 million civil money penalty against American Express National Bank for significant deficiencies in its Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program.
The OCC determined that the bank failed to establish and maintain a BSA/AML compliance program reasonably designed to assure and monitor compliance with the BSA and its implementing regulations.

Deficiencies included inadequate resources, systemic internal control gaps, weak independent testing, and insufficient BSA/AML training, leading to a failure to timely identify and report approximately $13 billion of suspected trade-based money laundering activity over the past decade.

articles.headline: OCC Issues Prohibition Orders Against Individuals for Embezzlement

Christopher Organista, a Former Operations Processor at the La Mirada, California Operations Center of U.S. Bank National Association, was prohibited for embezzling approximately $194,131 in bank customer funds.

articles.headline: BIS Extends Suspension of Affiliates Rule to January 10, 2027
body: The U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) published a final rule in the Federal Register on November 9, 2026, extending the suspension of its 'Affiliates Rule' through January 10, 2027.

The Affiliates Rule, originally issued on September 29, 2025, would extend Entity List and Military End User (MEU) List restrictions to non-U.S. entities that are 50 percent or more owned, individually or in aggregate, by listed parties.
This extension averts the rule's scheduled return on November 10, 2026, and maintains the pause on its implementation, which could otherwise restrict thousands of Chinese companies.

articles.headline: WuXi AppTec Removed from DoD Chinese Military Company List
body: WuXi AppTec has been removed from the Department of Defense's (DoD) so-called 1260H list under the U.S. National Defense Authorization Act, according to a notice published in the Federal Register on November 9, 2026.
The delisting follows a preliminary injunction won by WuXi AppTec in August, which temporarily blocked the U.S. government from enforcing its designation.

However, the notice explicitly states that the removal is 'without prejudice to relisting the company on additional or supplementary grounds,' indicating the possibility of future redesignation as the company's court case with the DoD is ongoing.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
